The Abkal: Suburba's divers, keepers of the Cortex, and the slums' way into Abzu.
The Cabiri: the slum fraternity of mechanics and rogue engineers who believe nothing has a final form.
The Coterie: the masked crime syndicate that rules Suburba's underworld and its vice.
Deshret: the last city, built downward into the earth after the surface burned.
The four tiers of Deshret, from the slums under the surface down to the palaces at the bottom.
Diving: going into Abzu, the Matrix, which most of the city treats as something closer to a spirit realm than a machine.
Words your character would know, from Abzu to yeoman.
The nine families who rule Deshret from the deepest floors, and how their titles and bastards work.
The Six Guilds: the city's great monopolies, their patron Saints, and the particles their members wear.
House Amari: keepers of the only real garden in Deshret, and the city's supplier of the real thing.
House Drepane: devoted servants of Symphony's digital gods, who live for beauty, drama, and spectacle.
House Kadesh: the truest believers in the city, who carve their faith into their own flesh.
House Morcant: masked, nameless, and somehow tied to death.
House Qamarat: owners of the crystals that power the city, the richest House, and very aware of it.
House Rook: the youngest Great House, raised up from the city watch, where nobody cares about your birth until you have served.
House Valcora: restless pilots who own the city's largest air fleet, and the only House that would rather go up.
House Varga: the feral nobles who keep the city's great hunting ground and breed the stock that splicing needs.
House Vesalius: the ancient, beautiful, and coldly polite rulers of Mythos.
The Kolkhos: the farmers' collective that feeds much of Suburba, and can turn a farm shift into a militia in minutes.
The four languages of Deshret: Shinar, Babble, Harran, and Nisabic.
Law and order in Deshret: a turf war between the state, the Church, the guilds, and the underworld.
What everyday life is like in Deshret, from housing and food to status, sex, drugs, and music.
What Deshret runs on and is made of: crystal power, synfuel, synthetic cloth, and slum woodwork.
Mythos: the guild that owns your body, and heals, augments, splices, and modifies it.
The Ophirian League: Suburba's salvage traders, a respectable professional association, and a cartel.
The Outriders: the guild that crosses into the scorched surface and brings back what the city cannot make.
Pegasus: the unseen guild. It votes, it tithes, and nobody has ever met a member.
The Church of the Nine: the city's one faith, what counts as sin, and how splintering brings the dead back.
The nine Saints: the Founders of Deshret, what each stands for, and how people wear them.
The eight Seals: holy shapes of broken and unbroken lines, and what people wear them for.
Sepulchre: the Church in a guild's seat, keeper of splintering and hunter of tech heresy.
Splicers: people with non-human DNA, from a pair of cat ears to a full animal head.
Symphony: the guild of everything the city sees, hears, and believes, run by gods who live in the Matrix.
Technology in Deshret: what the Church allows, what it forbids, and why a musket can share a room with a modern rifle.
The Hum: the sound that runs through the whole city, and what people believe it is.
Vulcani: the forge guild, where the craft itself is a form of worship, and every side of a war buys from the same catalogue.

sections.title: inventory
sections.body:
|winventory|n

Show your carried and held items. Aliases: |winv|n and |wi|n.

sections.title: wear
sections.body:
|wwear <clothing/armor>|n

Put on carried clothing or armor. Alias: |wdon|n.

sections.title: remove
sections.body:
|wremove <clothing/armor>|n

Take off worn clothing or armor. Alias: |wdoff|n.

sections.title: toggle
sections.body:

Change a two-state garment. Alias: |wadjust|n.

sections.body:

sections.body:

sections.title: unwield
sections.body:
|wunwield [<weapon>]|n

Move a held weapon into your inventory. Alias: |wstash|n.

sections.title: draw
sections.body:
|wdraw [<weapon>]|n
|wdraw from <cistern>|n

Draw a weapon from worn storage, or work a cistern pump in the room. Weapon
aliases: |wunsheathe|n and |wunholster|n.

sections.title: sheathe
sections.body:
|wsheathe [<weapon>] [in/into/on <rig>]|n

Put a held weapon into compatible worn storage. Aliases: |wsheath|n and |wholster|n.

sections.title: freehands
sections.body:
|wfreehands|n

Put all held objects into your inventory. Alias: |wfh|n.

sections.title: frisk
sections.body:
|wfrisk <character>|n

Search a compliant or subdued character's carried gear. Alias: |wpatdown|n.

For guns, see |whelp firearms|n and |whelp firearm modifications|n.
For clothing, see |whelp tailoring|n.

topic.summary: Weave cloth and turn a carried bolt into one finished garment.

sections.title: Recommended workflow
sections.body:
1. Open the garment designer with |wtailor <bolt>|n or |wtailor/web <bolt>|n.
2. Set a real name, examined description, worn appearance, and coverage. These four fields are required.
3. Add optional search aliases, fashion details, disguise shaping, and action messages.
4. Add appearance B if the garment can open, close, raise, lower, or otherwise switch configuration. Unchanged B fields inherit appearance A.
5. Use Preview. It shows the wearer, interaction target, and room-observer lines produced by the same renderer used in play.
6. Finalize only when the proof reads correctly. Finalizing consumes the bolt whether the craft succeeds or the work falls apart.

After finalization the strings live on the garment. |wtailor <garment>|n opens the garment record and reads every field back exactly as it was set.

Action messages use one reliable form: start with |w$N|n and mark the action as |w.verb|n.

|w$N .slip into $p $I.|n
|w$N .tip $p $I toward $T.|n

Put-on, take-off, and appearance-switch messages have no target. Only the interaction message accepts target tokens. If it uses one, the command in play is |wtease <garment> at <person>|n. Quotes and apostrophes are allowed. Write |w$$|n for a literal dollar sign.

Worn descriptions are appearance prose, not actions. They may use wearer and garment tokens, but never target tokens or |w.verb|n.

See |whelp tokens|n for the complete token table.

sections.title: loom
sections.body:
|wloom [<process>]|n

Open the loom menu. Give a process to start it.

sections.title: loom status
sections.body:
|wloom status|n

Check the work at the loom.

sections.title: loom claim
sections.body:
|wloom claim|n

Collect finished cloth from the loom.

sections.title: tailor
sections.body:
|wtailor [<bolt>]|n

Open the garment designer. Give a carried bolt to use it.

The in-game Preview option includes examined text, appearance A and B, put-on, take-off, interaction, and both appearance-switch messages.

sections.title: tailor garment
sections.body:
|wtailor <garment>|n

Read back a finished garment's authored strings exactly as they were set, including the rendered lines a wearer, target, and room will see. This is read-only; nothing on the garment changes.

With no argument, |wtailor|n opens the only carried bolt, or offers the carried garments when there is no bolt.

sections.title: clothing token
sections.body:
|wuse clothing token|n

Open the starting wardrobe designer. Finishing the garment uses the token.
A new character gets four tokens during the |w@newbie|n tour, and they only
work there: make your starting clothes before you finish the tour.

sections.title: tailor/web
sections.body:
|wtailor/web [<bolt>]|n

Open the web editor for a carried bolt.

The proof pane updates from unsaved text and reports invalid grammar before you save it.

sections.title: tailor/web modify
sections.body:
|wtailor/web modify <garment>|n

Open the web editor for a tailored garment.

For wearing clothing, see |whelp inventory|n.
For text formatting, see |whelp tokens|n.

topic.summary: Talk, and write what your character does.

sections.title: say
sections.body:
|wsay <message>|n
|w"<message>|n
|w'<message>|n

Say something out loud to everyone in the room.

Example: |w"Nice night for it.|n

sections.title: to
sections.body:
|wto <person> <message>|n

Say something out loud to the room, aimed at one person. Name them the way
you see them.

Example: |wto lissome One root-fibre tea, please.|n

sections.title: whisper
sections.body:
|wwhisper <person>[, <person> ...] = <message>|n

Speak quietly to one or more people. Others in the room may catch part of it.

sections.title: pose
sections.body:
|wpose <text>|n
|w.<text>|n

Write what you do in the first person and leave your name out. The game puts
your name in front and fixes your first verb for each reader. Put a dot in
front of any later verb that needs the same fix. Your |wI|n, |wmy|n, and
|wme|n become your pronouns for everyone else.

Example: |w.wave at Prismodal and .give them a nudge.|n

  You see:     You wave at Prismodal and give them a nudge.
  Others see:  Sol waves at Prismodal and gives them a nudge.

The person you name reads "you" in place of their name.

Name people the way you see them: their short description, the name you gave
them with |wrecog|n, or the end of their description, such as
|wthe willowy woman|n. When two people match, put a number in front:
|w1-willowy woman|n or |w2-willowy woman|n.

sections.title: comma pose
sections.body:
|w,<text>|n
|wpose ,<text>|n

Start with a comma to open the pose your own way. Your name does not go in
front, and your first verb stays as you typed it. Your first |wI|n becomes
your name.

Example: |w,Grinning, I .lean back in my chair.|n

  Others see:  Grinning, Sol leans back in her chair.

sections.title: emote
sections.body:
|wemote <text>|n
|wemote ,<text>|n

Write what you do in the third person. Everyone reads the text as you typed
it, after your name. Start with a comma to leave your name out. Names of
people in the room change for each reader, as in a pose.

Example: |wemote waves at Prismodal.|n

sections.title: language
sections.body:
|wlanguage [<language>]|n

List your languages, or choose the one you speak.

sections.title: looc
sections.body:
|wlooc <message>|n

Send an out-of-character message to the room.

sections.title: @afk
sections.body:
|w@afk [<minutes>]|n
|w@bak|n

Tell the room that you are away from the keyboard, for up to 99 minutes or
with no time limit. |w@bak|n tells the room you are back. Any other command
also ends it. Aliases: |w@away|n and |w@unafk|n.

sections.title: tease
sections.body:
|wtease <worn clothing> [at <person>]|n

Use the move written into a piece of worn clothing. Alias: |wflaunt|n.

To read a syntax line, see |whelp syntax|n.
For your appearance, see |whelp description|n.
For small groups inside a room, see |whelp places|n.
For poses that stay on the room, see |whelp room poses|n.
For OOC channels, see |whelp channels|n.
